summary:
Nimbus Nova is a cooperative Minecraft mission trainer that puts students in charge of a Mars outpost, a lunar expedition, or a spacecraft in distress. Across six missions, students take roles such as power engineer, life support specialist, and pilot. Each role sees different readings, so the crew has to share information before making shared decisions.

In The Darkening Sky, measurements from NASA’s Opportunity rover shape the drop in solar output during a Martian dust storm. Students must decide whether to keep research running, spend a limited backup reserve, or conserve power for oxygen production. Other missions ask crews to build radiation shielding, repair a hull breach, land on the Moon, or keep crops alive after a pipe fails.

Students carry out their decisions at working equipment in the game. They trace circuits, adjust water and airflow, and carry repair supplies to damaged systems. Teachers can choose a mission, invite students with a join code, pause for discussion, and review a debrief showing what the crew achieved and how their choices affected the outcome.

The game gives students a concrete way to see why safety and scientific goals sometimes compete, and how crew communication helps keep a mission on track.
details:
Nimbus Nova is a cooperative Minecraft mission trainer for younger students. A teacher selects one of six missions and opens a session. Students join with a code, choose a role, and follow in-game waypoints to their equipment. A power engineer sees the battery and can change what draws electricity. A life support specialist watches the air supply. Each player has part of the picture, so the crew has to share readings before deciding what to do.

In *The Darkening Sky*, observations from NASA’s Opportunity rover shape how much solar output drops during a Martian dust storm. Students have to decide whether to keep research running, spend a limited backup reserve, or save power for oxygen production. In other missions, they compare radiation readings before taking shelter, place a repair plate into a spacecraft’s hull breach, or adjust irrigation and lighting to keep crops alive. The game uses simplified resource values and compressed timelines so students can see the effects of their decisions during one session.

The teacher dashboard lets teachers choose missions, pause for discussion, view a student’s game, and review a debrief. The debrief gives the class a concrete decision to revisit. For example, when did the crew have enough evidence to shift power away from research, and what did that choice cost? Our goal is to give students practice explaining decisions from evidence, coordinating across roles, and balancing safety with scientific work.

We built the mod for *Minecraft Java Edition 26.3* using *Java 25, Fabric, and Gradle. The teacher dashboard uses **Node.js, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript*. We created custom maps, equipment, and interfaces, and tested the missions on a Mac through fullscreen play and automated Minecraft tests.

We chose Minecraft because familiar actions like walking, building, and sharing items give students a way into unfamiliar engineering problems. We designed untimed preparation, visible waypoints, and short station tasks so new players can learn their controls before the crew has to make decisions under pressure.
projectRefs: The Planetary Society — Opportunity’s pre-storm solar output
